claim: Indirect flight muscles (IFMs) are the major muscles in the adult thorax that power flight.
source: Indirect flight muscles (IFMs) are the major muscles in the adult thorax that power flight (Gunage et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement directly from the text with a supporting citation.

claim: IFMs are more similar to vertebrate muscles than most Drosophila muscles because IFMs are fibrillar as opposed to tubular muscles.
source: IFMs are more similar to vertebrate muscles than most Drosophila muscles, because IFMs are fibrillar as opposed to tubular muscles such as the adult leg muscle.
evidence: This is a direct comparison stated in the text.

claim: Fibrillar muscles are made up of myofibers, which in turn contain hundreds of myofibrils.
source: Fibrillar muscles are made up of myofibers, which in turn contain hundreds of myofibrils.
evidence: This is a structural description stated directly in the text.

claim: In the IFMs, sarcomeres form simultaneously along the length of each myofibril during pupal development.
source: In the IFMs, sarcomeres form simultaneously along the length of each myofibril during pupal development (Weitkunat et al., 2014)
evidence: This is a statement about sarcomere formation with a supporting citation.

claim: Sarcomeres elongate by growth from the actin pointed ends.
source: In the IFMs, sarcomeres form simultaneously along the length of each myofibril during pupal development (Weitkunat et al., 2014) and then elongate by growth from the actin pointed ends, and widen by circumferential addition (Mardahl-Dumesnil and Fowler, 2001; Shwartz et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about sarcomere growth with supporting citations.

claim: Sarcomeres widen by circumferential addition.
source: In the IFMs, sarcomeres form simultaneously along the length of each myofibril during pupal development (Weitkunat et al., 2014) and then elongate by growth from the actin pointed ends, and widen by circumferential addition (Mardahl-Dumesnil and Fowler, 2001; Shwartz et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about sarcomere widening with supporting citations.

claim: At the ends of each myofibril are modified terminal Z-lines (MTZ), which contain sites of integrin adhesion to the epidermal tendon cell.
source: At the ends of each myofibril are modified terminal Z-lines (MTZ), which contain sites of integrin adhesion to the epidermal tendon cell.
evidence: This is a structural description stated directly in the text.

claim: The myofibril and tendon cell membranes form finger-like protrusions that interdigitate with one another.
source: The myofibril and tendon cell membranes form finger-like protrusions that interdigitate with one another (hereafter referred to as interdigitations).
evidence: This is a structural description stated directly in the text.

claim: The attachment sites in IFMs appear by electron microscopy more complex and larger than those in larval muscles, with ~1 µm separating plasma membrane from first sarcomere versus 0.1–0.5 µm.
source: The attachment sites in IFMs appear by electron microscopy more complex and larger than those in larval muscles, with ~1 µm separating plasma membrane from first sarcomere versus 0.1–0.5 µm (Reedy and Beall, 1993; Tepass and Hartenstein, 1994).
evidence: This is a comparative measurement with supporting citations.

claim: IFMs contract 200 times per second.

evidence: This is a quantitative measurement with a supporting citation.

claim: Larval muscles contract once every ~5 s during crawling.
source: Furthermore, IFMs contract 200 times per second (Fry et al., 2003), whereas larval muscles contract once every ~5 s during crawling (Crisp et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement with a supporting citation.

claim: Focal Adhesion Kinase (FAK), RSU1, tensin and vinculin are not required for viability of the fly.

claim: The adult indirect flight muscles of Drosophila are an excellent system to identify functions for integrin-associated proteins (IAPs) that are not essential for viability.
